auditScope: Sample audit of 12 spec files from different components and categories

violations.issue: Uses @playwright/test directly instead of persistent-context. Misses auth context fixture that handles storageState injection.
violations.impact: Tests run without proper auth initialization; fails at login checks

violations.issue: Uses @playwright/test directly instead of persistent-context. Misses auth context fixture.
violations.impact: Tests run without proper auth initialization

violations.issue: Hardcoded style guide URL instead of using resolveComponentUrl() utility. Breaks in non-local envs where fixtures are deployed elsewhere.
violations.impact: Tests will fail in qa/uat/prod if fixture deployment strategy changes; violates DRY principle

violations.issue: Hardcoded URL in 34 tests instead of resolveComponentUrl(). Massive DRY violation and fragility.
violations.impact: 34 hardcoded URLs across one file; fragile, unmaintainable, violates DRY

violations.issue: ConsoleCapture is started and stopped but NEVER attached to the report via attachConsoleCapture(). Captured errors exist only in memory and are lost after test ends.
violations.impact: Console errors are captured but lost; report shows no diagnostic data even when errors occur

violations.issue: ConsoleCapture used but NEVER attached to report via attachConsoleCapture(). Diagnostic data is lost.
violations.impact: Console diagnostics lost; report enhancement doesn't happen

violations.issue: ConsoleCapture imported but used pattern analysis required. Need to verify whether capture is attached to report.
violations.fix:
import { ConsoleCapture } from '../../../utils/infra/console-capture';
import { attachConsoleCapture } from '../../../utils/infra/report-enhancer';
violations.impact: May lose diagnostic data if attachConsoleCapture not called

violations.issue: Uses raw expect() assertions instead of assert-utils wrapper functions like isVisible(). Cannot reuse, not soft-assertion capable.
violations.impact: Cannot leverage soft assertions, consistency, or error handling from assert-utils

violations.issue: Tests call POM methods (pom.navigate, pom.getRoot) before explicit loginToAEMAuthor(). POM's navigate() doesn't call login, so auth is missing during initial navigation.
violations.impact: Tests may fail with 401 Unauthorized or missing admin content before beforeEach completes

violations.issue: Uses raw page.click() instead of clickElement() from action-utils. Missing error handling, retry logic, and detached element handling.
violations.impact: No automatic retry on detached elements; brittle to race conditions

violations.issue: Hardcoded waitForTimeout() calls scattered throughout. Should centralize timeout constants or use more robust wait strategies.
violations.impact: Magic numbers; hard to maintain; brittle if animation timings change

violations.issue: Defines helper function with CSS selectors instead of using ButtonPage POM methods. Duplicates logic; reduces reusability across specs.
violations.impact: Selector logic duplicated; harder to maintain; POM pattern not fully leveraged

roadmap.description: Replace @playwright/test imports with persistent-context in feature-banner.author.spec.ts and form-field-text.author.spec.ts
Replace hardcoded URLs with resolveComponentUrl() in feature-banner and form-field-text specs. Feature-banner: 10 URLs; form-field-text: 34 URLs.
roadmap.dryRunEstimate: 2h per file — feature-banner 10 replacements; form-field-text 34 replacements

roadmap.description: Add attachConsoleCapture(testInfo, capture) calls in navigation.author.spec.ts and accordion.author.spec.ts to ensure console diagnostics reach the report.
roadmap.dryRunEstimate: 30 min per file — 2 test methods per file that use ConsoleCapture

roadmap.description: Replace raw page.click() calls with clickElement() from action-utils in navigation.author.spec.ts (10 instances). Adds retry logic and detached element handling.
roadmap.dryRunEstimate: 1.5h — ~10 click() calls to replace with clickElement() wrapper

roadmap.description: Replace raw expect() assertions with assert-utils functions (isVisible, expectElementToHaveText, etc.) in statistic.author.spec.ts. Enables soft assertions and consistent error handling.
roadmap.dryRunEstimate: 2h — ~20 expect() calls to wrap with assert-utils equivalents

roadmap.description: Add explicit loginToAEMAuthor() call in test body (not just beforeEach) in footer.author.spec.ts before POM navigation calls.
roadmap.dryRunEstimate: 20 min — add 1 line per test that calls pom.navigate()

roadmap.description: Replace hardcoded waitForTimeout values in accordion.author.spec.ts (11 instances) with named constants. Centralizes magic numbers.
roadmap.dryRunEstimate: 1h — define 3-4 timeout constants and replace 11 uses

roadmap.description: Move inline selector functions (e.g., primaryBtn in button.visual.spec.ts) into ButtonPage POM methods. Centralizes selector logic.
roadmap.dryRunEstimate: 1.5h — extract 1 helper function to POM, update 6 call sites

sampleFixes.explanation: Fixes 2 critical violations: (1) Changes import from @playwright/test to persistent-context to enable auth context fixture reuse; (2) Replaces hardcoded style guide URLs with resolveComponentUrl(), making the spec environment-agnostic and maintainable.

sampleFixes.violation: V-005 (Console Capture not attached) + V-010 (raw page.click)
sampleFixes.explanation: Fixes 2 high-severity violations: (1) Adds await attachConsoleCapture(testInfo, capture) to ensure console errors are attached to the Playwright report for analysis; (2) Replaces raw .click() calls with clickElement() which provides automatic retry on detached elements, error handling, and page-closed checks.

sampleFixes.violation: V-006 (Console Capture not attached) + V-011 (hardcoded timeouts)
sampleFixes.explanation: Fixes 2 violations: (1) Adds await attachConsoleCapture(testInfo, capture) so console diagnostics reach the report; (2) Replaces magic numbers (300, 500, 1000) with named constants (EXPAND_ANIMATION, NAVIGATION_SETTLE) for maintainability and clarity.

Replaces raw expect() assertions with assert-utils equivalents (isVisible, expectElementToHaveCount). This enables soft assertions, consistent error handling, and leverages the framework's wrapper functions for maintainability.

sampleFixes.violation: V-002 + V-004 (Import + URL Resolution - partial fix)
sampleFixes.explanation: Fixes critical violations: (1) Changes import to persistent-context; (2) Centralizes URL resolution in test.beforeAll() and reuses formFieldTextUrl variable across all 34 tests, eliminating hardcoded URLs and massive DRY violation. Apply pattern to remaining 32 tests in the file.

keyFindings: Critical: 2 specs import @playwright/test instead of persistent-context — breaks auth context reuse
Critical: 44 hardcoded style guide URLs across 2 specs — massive DRY violation and environment fragility
Critical: 2 specs capture console errors but never attach to report — diagnostic data is lost
High: 1 spec uses ~10 raw page.click() calls instead of clickElement() wrapper — missing error handling and retry logic
High: 1 spec uses ~20 raw expect() instead of assert-utils — cannot leverage soft assertions or framework error handling
High: 1 spec has login in beforeEach but tests call POM methods before implicit login completion — potential 401 errors
Medium: 1 spec has 11 hardcoded timeout values — magic numbers reduce maintainability
Medium: 1 spec defines helper selector function instead of adding to POM — duplicates logic, reduces reusability
Estimated fix time: 19 hours to address all violations in sampled files
Full repo fix (171 files) likely 2-3x effort: ~40-60 hours for comprehensive refactoring
recommendedApproach: Phase 1 (4h): Fix critical imports and URL resolution — 2 files, highest impact
Phase 2 (4h): Fix critical console capture attachment — 2 files, enables better reporting
Phase 3 (6h): Replace action/assert utils in high-priority files — foundation for other refactors
Phase 4 (2h): Fix login placement and timeout constants — medium-priority improvements
Phase 5 (3h): Generalize fixes and apply to remaining 159 files — batch processing approach
